First listed 2025-12-22 · episode or wrap

Steve Eisman's Masterclass on the 2008 Financial Crisis (Part Two) | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 39

Eisman traces crisis contagion through retained mortgage exposures and CDS, criticizes underwriting due diligence, and argues that post-crisis capital and liquidity rules made large banks safer. He explains SVB as concentrated uninsured funding combined with duration risk, then favors targeted regulatory easing and consolidation. Primary records support the core SVB mechanism and substantial post-crisis recapitalization. Important qualifications concern HTM accounting, blanket bailout protection, nonrandom due-diligence samples and claims that SVB posed no systemic danger. The concluding multi-year bank outlook remains conditional and only partly observable.

How he reasons here

  • Examine where distributed credit risk ultimately remains.
  • A hedge adds counterparty dependence rather than eliminating all risk.
  • Distinguish asset credit risk, duration risk and liability concentration.
  • Assess regulation through behavior and unintended consequences, not only stated intentions.
  • Separate earnings pressure from immediate liquidity failure, while recognizing economic capital losses.
